title: Come Let Us Lift Our Voices High
description: Come Let Us Lift Our Voices High in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 12 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book III, prepared for the Lord's Supper, hymn 21, headed “The triumphal feast for Christ's victory over sin, and death, and hell”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come let us lift our voi-ces high, High as our joys a-rise, And join the songs a-bove the sky, Where plea-sure nev-er dies.

lines: Come let us lift our voices high,
And join the songs above the sky,
Jesus, the God that fought and bled,
That rose, and at his chariot-wheels
Dragg'd all the powers of hell.
Jesus the God invites us here
The Lord! how glorious is his face!
And O what melting words he says
"For you, the children of my love,
"These are the wounds for you I bore,
"When I came down to free your souls
And plung'd it in my heart;
"When hell and all its spiteful powers
"To rescue those dear lives of yours
"But while I bled, and groan'd, and dy'd,
"High on my cross I hung, and spy'd
"Now you must triumph at my feast,
Victorious God! what can we pay
We would devote our hearts away
We give thee, Lord, our highest praise,
But themes so infinite as these

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
